newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerian court sentences three fugitives to death.
newsitem.headline: Algerian court sentences three fugitives to death.

text.p: An Algerian court sentenced three Moslem fundamentalists to death in absentia for "belonging to an armed terrorist group aiming to spread death", the official Algerian news agency APS said on Wednesday.

The three men, still on the run, were sentenced by Medea criminal court on Tuesday. Three others facing the same charges were acquitted, the agency said, without detailing whether they were in court for the trial.
Medea, 60-km (40-miles) southwest of Algiers, has been a focal point of trials in the five-year-old conflict between security forces and Moslem guerrillas.
Last Monday, the court there sentenced six men to death in their absence. They were charged with belonging to "armed terrorist groups, pre-meditated murder, ambushes, and arson".
On December 1, APS reported that the same court had condemned to death 23 members of a "terrorist" group -- all on the run.
APS on Tuesday said a criminal court in Tlemcen, 440-km (275-miles), west of Algiers, convicted 12 men, also on the run, to death for involvement in guerrilla activities.
More than 1,200 Moslem fundamentalits have been condemned to death, mostly in absentia, since 1993 when Algerian courts started trials of activists.
About 60,000 people have died in Algeria's violence since 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a commanding lead.
